options: старуха
старухи
старухе
старухой
cases.translation: And the old woman handed the watch back to him.
cases.explain: "Старуха" is the subject of the verb "протянула" (handed back), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Ведь надобно же, чтобы у всякого ___ было хоть одно такое место, где б его пожалели.
options: человек
человека
человеку
человеком
cases.translation: After all, every man needs at least one such place where he'd be pitied.
cases.explain: The preposition "у" (expressing possession, "in the case of") always governs the genitive case, giving "человека."

cases.sentence: Замиранием сердца и нервной дрожью подошел он к преогромнейшему ___.
options: дом
дома
дому
домом
cases.translation: With a sinking heart and nervous trembling, he approached the enormous house.
cases.explain: The preposition "к" (toward) always governs the dative case, giving "дому."

cases.sentence: Тогда я, четырнадцатилетнюю дочь имея, ___ свою предложил.
options: рука
руки
руке
руку
cases.translation: Then I, having a fourteen-year-old daughter, offered her my hand (in marriage).
cases.explain: "Предложил" (offered) is a transitive verb whose direct object takes the accusative case: "руку."

cases.sentence: Он благополучно избегнул встречи со своей ___ на лестнице.
options: хозяйка
хозяйки
хозяйке
хозяйкой
cases.translation: He successfully avoided meeting his landlady on the stairs.
cases.explain: The preposition "с" (with) here governs the instrumental case, giving "хозяйкой."

cases.sentence: Наконец ему стало душно и тесно в этой желтой ___, похожей на шкаф или на сундук.
options: коморка
коморки
коморкой
коморке
cases.translation: At last he felt stifled and cramped in that yellow little room, which resembled a cupboard or a trunk.
cases.explain: The preposition "в" marking location governs the prepositional case, giving "коморке."

reading.ru: В начале июля, в чрезвычайно жаркое время, под вечер, один молодой человек вышел из своей коморки, которую нанимал от жильцов в СМ Переулкин, на улицу и медленно, как бы в нерешимости, отправился к сну мосту.
reading.question: What is the young man doing at the very beginning of the story?
options: Leaving his rented room and walking hesitantly toward a bridge
Arriving home from work
Meeting his mother at the train station
Running from the police
reading.correct: Leaving his rented room and walking hesitantly toward a bridge
reading.explain: The opening sentence describes him leaving his tiny rented room on a hot evening and slowly, as if in indecision, heading toward a bridge.

reading.ru: Другое дело при встрече с иными знакомыми или с прежними товарищами, с которыми вообще он не любил встречаться.
reading.question: How does the young man feel about running into old acquaintances or former friends?
options: It was another matter entirely — he specifically disliked meeting them
He was eager to catch up with everyone he knew
He no longer had any acquaintances at all
He believed he owed them all money
reading.correct: It was another matter entirely — he specifically disliked meeting them
reading.explain: The text says meeting acquaintances or old friends was "another matter," as he generally disliked encountering them.

reading.ru: Немного спустя дверь приотворилась на крошечную щелочку.
reading.question: How does the old woman (pawnbroker) respond when the young man knocks on her door?
options: She opens the door only a tiny crack
She throws the door wide open at once
She refuses to answer at all
She calls for help from a neighbor
reading.correct: She opens the door only a tiny crack
reading.explain: After a moment, the door opens only "a tiny little crack," showing her caution.

reading.ru: И старуха протянула ему обратно часы.
reading.question: What does the old pawnbroker do after quoting her low price for the young man's watch?
options: She hands the watch back to him
She keeps the watch and gives him no money
She smashes the watch
She offers to buy it for double the price
reading.correct: She hands the watch back to him
reading.explain: After naming her price of a rouble and a half, the old woman hands the watch back to him.

reading.ru: Главное, грязно, пакостно, гадко, гадко.
reading.question: How does the young man describe his own feelings about the plan he is contemplating?
options: He calls it dirty, vile, and disgusting
He calls it clever and admirable
He feels completely indifferent about it
He feels proud and confident
reading.correct: He calls it dirty, vile, and disgusting
reading.explain: He repeats to himself that, mainly, it is "dirty, nasty, vile, vile," showing his self-disgust at the plan forming in his mind.

reading.ru: Он беспрерывно вглядывал на чиновника, конечно, и потому еще, что сам тот упорно смотрел на него, и видно было, что тому очень хотелось начать разговор.
reading.question: What does the young man notice about the official (Marmeladov) sitting nearby in the tavern?
options: The official keeps staring at him and seems eager to start a conversation
The official is fast asleep at his table
The official is arguing loudly with the bartender
The official completely ignores everyone around him
reading.correct: The official keeps staring at him and seems eager to start a conversation
reading.explain: The young man keeps looking at the official partly because the official himself stares back, clearly wanting to strike up a conversation.

reading.ru: Он налил стаканчик, выпил и задумался.
reading.question: What does the official (Marmeladov) do with his drink before falling into thought?
options: He pours a glass, drinks it, and becomes lost in thought
He refuses to drink and pushes the glass away
He spills the drink on the table
He offers the drink to the young man first
reading.correct: He pours a glass, drinks it, and becomes lost in thought
reading.explain: Marmeladov pours himself a small glass, drinks it, and becomes thoughtful, right before the narrator notes hay stuck to his clothes.

reading.ru: Милостивый государь, милостивый государь, Ведь надобно же, чтобы у всякого человека было хоть одно такое место, где б его пожалели.
reading.question: What does Marmeladov say every person needs, according to his speech?
options: At least one place where he can be pitied
A large sum of money
A respectable government position
A wife who never scolds him
reading.correct: At least one place where he can be pitied
reading.explain: Marmeladov declares that every man needs at least one such place where he would be pitied.

reading.ru: Можете судить по тому, до какой степени ее бедствия доходили, что она, образованная и воспитанная, и фамилией известной, за меня согласилась пойти.
reading.question: What does Marmeladov say about why his wife Katerina Ivanovna agreed to marry him?
options: Her misfortunes were so severe that she, educated and from a known family, agreed to marry him out of desperation
She married him because she loved him deeply from the start
She married him purely for his wealth
Her family arranged the marriage against her will
reading.correct: Her misfortunes were so severe that she, educated and from a known family, agreed to marry him out of desperation
reading.explain: Marmeladov says one can judge the depth of her misfortunes by the fact that she, educated and of a known family, agreed to marry him.

reading.ru: Но не вините, не вините, милостивый государь, не вините.
reading.question: What does Marmeladov repeatedly beg Raskolnikov not to do regarding his wife's harsh words?
options: Not to blame her
To arrest her
To report her to the church
To lend her more money
reading.correct: Not to blame her
reading.explain: Marmeladov repeats three times, "But do not blame her, do not blame her, my dear sir, do not blame her," excusing his wife's harshness as coming from her suffering.

reading.ru: Раскольников слушал внимательно.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov react as Marmeladov continues telling his story?
options: He listens attentively
He gets up and leaves immediately
He starts arguing with Marmeladov
He falls asleep at the table
reading.correct: He listens attentively
reading.explain: The text simply states that Raskolnikov listened attentively to Marmeladov's confession.

reading.ru: Вам, может быть, все это в смех, как и прочим, и только беспокоя я вас глупостью и всех этих незерных подробностей домашней жизни моей.
reading.question: What does Marmeladov worry Raskolnikov might think about his long, detailed confession?
options: That it's all a joke to him, as it is to others
That it's the most fascinating story he's ever heard
That he should publish it in a newspaper
That he is lying about everything
reading.correct: That it's all a joke to him, as it is to others
reading.explain: Marmeladov worries that, like everyone else, Raskolnikov finds all this a laughing matter and that he is only bothering him with foolish domestic details.

reading.ru: Скорби, скорби искал я на дне его, Скорби и слез и вкусил, и обрел.
reading.question: In the verses Marmeladov recites, what does he claim to have sought and found at the bottom of his cup?
options: Sorrow and tears
Wealth and fame
Forgetfulness and joy
Nothing at all
reading.correct: Sorrow and tears
reading.explain: The recited verse says he sought sorrow at the bottom of the cup, and tasted and found sorrow and tears.

reading.ru: Они вошли со двора и прошли в четвертый этаж.
reading.question: Where do Raskolnikov and Marmeladov go after leaving the tavern?
options: Up to the fourth floor of Marmeladov's building, entering from the courtyard
To the police station
To a restaurant for dinner
Back to the pawnbroker's apartment
reading.correct: Up to the fourth floor of Marmeladov's building, entering from the courtyard
reading.explain: They enter from the courtyard and go up to the fourth floor, where Marmeladov's family lives.

reading.ru: И она бросилась его обыскивать.
reading.question: What does Marmeladov's wife do the moment they arrive at the apartment?
options: She rushes to search his pockets for money
She embraces him warmly
She offers him tea
She faints from exhaustion
reading.correct: She rushes to search his pockets for money
reading.explain: Katerina Ivanovna immediately rushes to search Marmeladov's pockets, and he obediently spreads his arms to help.

reading.ru: Ай да, Соня, какой колодец, однако ж, сумели выкопать и пользуются.
reading.question: What bitter remark is made about how the family benefits from Sonya's earnings?
options: That she has "dug a well" (a source of money) which the family now draws from
That she won money in a lottery
That she inherited money from a relative
That she found a generous employer
reading.correct: That she has "dug a well" (a source of money) which the family now draws from
reading.explain: The bitter remark compares Sonya's earnings to a well the family has dug and now uses for themselves.

reading.ru: Дура она!» — прибавил он громко.
reading.question: What does the speaker call the woman he is thinking about, right before deciding to go visit her that day?
options: A fool (дура)
A genius
A saint
A liar
reading.correct: A fool (дура)
reading.explain: He loudly adds, "She's a fool!" before resolving to go see her and talk that same day.

reading.ru: Письмо было большое, плотное, в два лота.
reading.question: How is the letter that Raskolnikov receives from his mother described?
options: Large and heavy, weighing two lots
Short and hastily scribbled
Torn and illegible
Written in a foreign language
reading.correct: Large and heavy, weighing two lots
reading.explain: The letter is described as large, thick, and weighing two lots (an old Russian unit of weight).

reading.ru: А тут поднялся проливной дождь.
reading.question: What additional misfortune makes Dunya's humiliating journey home even worse, according to the letter?
options: A torrential downpour begins during her uncovered-cart ride
She loses her luggage along the way
Her carriage breaks down completely
She becomes seriously ill with fever
reading.correct: A torrential downpour begins during her uncovered-cart ride
reading.explain: The letter recounts that on top of everything else, a torrential rain began during Dunya's humiliating ride in an uncovered cart.

reading.ru: Разумеется, мы сначала были очень поражены, так как все это произошло слишком скоро и неожиданно.
reading.question: How does the mother describe the family's reaction to Luzhin's sudden proposal?
options: They were very struck/surprised, since it happened too quickly and unexpectedly
They were completely indifferent to the news
They had been expecting it for years
They refused it immediately without any discussion
reading.correct: They were very struck/surprised, since it happened too quickly and unexpectedly
reading.explain: The mother writes that they were naturally very struck by the news, since everything happened too quickly and unexpectedly.

reading.ru: Потому не говорили, что, во-первых, это и само собой сделается впоследствии, он, наверное, без лишних слов сам предложит».
reading.question: What financial hope does the mother describe regarding Luzhin's future help for Raskolnikov?
options: That Luzhin will offer, without being asked, to employ and pay him
That Luzhin will give them a lump sum of cash immediately
That Luzhin will pay off all the family's debts at once
That Luzhin will fund Raskolnikov's wedding
reading.correct: That Luzhin will offer, without being asked, to employ and pay him
reading.explain: The mother explains they hadn't mentioned it yet because it would surely happen on its own, with Luzhin offering the help himself without being asked.

reading.ru: Наконец ему стало душно и тесно в этой желтой коморке, похожей на шкаф или на сундук.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov feel in his small room after reading his mother's letter?
options: Suffocated and cramped, as if trapped in a cupboard or a trunk
Warm and perfectly comfortable
Sleepy and relaxed
Excited and ready to celebrate
reading.correct: Suffocated and cramped, as if trapped in a cupboard or a trunk
reading.explain: The text says he finally felt stifled and cramped in his yellow little room, which resembled a cupboard or a trunk.

reading.ru: Большой сундук на свой счет доставляет.
reading.question: According to the letter, what travel arrangement does Luzhin make at his own expense?
options: He pays to have a large trunk delivered
He books first-class train tickets
He hires a private carriage
He arranges a hotel room
reading.correct: He pays to have a large trunk delivered
reading.explain: The letter notes that Luzhin has taken the luggage upon himself and delivers a large trunk at his own expense.

reading.ru: Ну, Дуня-то что?» «Дунечка, милая, ведь я знаю вас.
reading.question: What does the mother fondly recall in her letter while addressing Dunya?
options: That she still knows and remembers her dear Dunechka well
That Dunya has forgotten her entirely
That Dunya never writes back
That Dunya has become a stranger to the family
reading.correct: That she still knows and remembers her dear Dunechka well
reading.explain: The mother affectionately addresses her, "Dunechka, my dear, I do know you," reflecting on how long it has been since they last met.

reading.ru: Тут мы и от Сонечки на жребия, пожалуй, не откажемся.
reading.question: What bitter comparison does Raskolnikov draw at the end of this section, about self-sacrifice?
options: He compares the family's willingness to accept Dunya's sacrificial marriage to Sonya's self-sacrifice
He compares his mother to a saint
He compares Luzhin to a hero
He decides to reject his family's help entirely
reading.correct: He compares the family's willingness to accept Dunya's sacrificial marriage to Sonya's self-sacrifice
reading.explain: Raskolnikov bitterly reflects that they would not even refuse a sacrifice like Sonechka's, drawing a parallel between Dunya's planned marriage and Sonya's self-sacrifice.
